implementation: Optional fixed-scenario API and private-config provider CLI run actual coordinator, two provider services and two agents in separate processes. Real leases, HTTP transfer, Docker ingress, SQLite, mount faults and fencing drive every pass.

release.skipScope: Existing privileged tests require an explicitly disposable environment; the separate real guest driver passes without skips.

minimumNode.fullLocalGate: All tests passed, but V8 coverage JSON was truncated at position 327680. The existing narrow retry did not recognize it, so the gate failed closed. Full local minimum-Node coverage is not claimed. Hosted minimum-Node checks remain required.

disposableLinux.certification: Fresh current profile, all seven actual capabilities passed before drills.
disposableLinux.scope: Owned Debian 13 KVM guest with its own Docker daemon, dedicated new XFS disk, preloaded immutable image. No production certification or host-global changes.

documentation.browser: Actual desktop 1280px and phone 390px search/navigation/guide checks passed; no horizontal overflow. Owned server stopped, browser tab closed.

fixes.problem: Non-root provider administrative ambient capabilities caused Bubblewrap to reject SQLite workers.
fixes.change: Clear inheritable/ambient capabilities and set NoNewPrivs in the SQLite child before Bubblewrap; preserve provider state and sandbox restrictions.
fixes.evidence: Real migrations and SQLite work in every guest drill with the capability-bearing actual production provider.

fixes.problem: Provider umask 077 altered approved artifact file modes, causing verified release staging to fail.
fixes.change: Restore verified modes after exclusive file creation. All four allowed modes and exact bytes have a child-process regression under umask 077.
Bind setpriv, mount and umount executable bytes/permissions in host certification.

package.change: Proposal #273 adds exactly one optional JS/declaration pair; root browser entry stays unchanged.

boundaries: Portable takeover initializes only a fixed synthetic database on node B. It proves placement, artifact identity and credential/fence rejection; it does not establish database replication.
The separate stopped stateful placement proves control-store pinning, not live stateful failover.
No automatic supervisor leadership is included.
A current root-operated host certificate and explicit disposable authorization are required; production Railway remains uncertified.
Parent death or unconfirmed owned cleanup retains the host admission marker until ownership-verified cleanup. No automatic unlock or broad resource deletion.
Framework/native-tool changes invalidate old certificates; recertification is required.
